F01.answer:
The two most recent papers on Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) are:

[32] The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement, which presents a roadmap for RSI development including "improvement-execution autonomy, improvement-strategy autonomy, experience-acquisition autonomy, and environment-adaptation autonomy, to recursive meta-improvement," and examines RSI across different scenarios like scientific discovery, embodied intelligence, and software engineering [32].

[31] ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement, which proposes a benchmark-disjoint, contrastive, and modular framework for generalizable harness evolution that decomposes the evolvable harness into five functional modules (Agent Loop, Tool Use, Observation Management, Context Management, and Task Completion Detection) to solve challenges in generalizable harness RSI [31].

F02.question: Vad har hänt med GUI agents den senaste månaden?
F02.answer:
Recent developments in GUI agents over the past month include several new frameworks, benchmarks, and models that advance the field. 

Researchers have introduced TRACE, a training-free framework for trajectory-robust admission and coverage-aware evidence ordering that reduces inference latency and memory usage for GUI agents [21]. 

A new benchmark called MobilePA-Bench has been developed to evaluate mobile planner agents on complex real-world tasks, assessing sub-agent collaboration, memory usage, and skill usage across 13 functional domains and 212 realistic mobile tools [25].

Several new foundation models have been proposed, including UI-Mate, which integrates an environment-grounded training stack with in-context demonstration learning to improve long-horizon reliability, reaching 41.0% strict success on OSWorkerBench [29].

UI-Venus-2 has been introduced as a general-purpose foundation GUI agent designed to operate across mobile, web, and desktop environments through a unified closed-loop reasoning-action framework, with expanded coverage to more than 170 multilingual mobile apps and native desktop operating systems [30].

New benchmarks have also emerged to diagnose specific challenges: GUI-Primitives evaluates spatial reasoning failures in vision-language GUI grounding with 994-item contrastive instruction pairs over seven spatial relations [26], while AnTrap evaluates agent robustness against runtime anomalies in dynamic adversarial environments [27].

LLaDA-UI has been proposed as a block-wise diffusion vision-language GUI agent that substantially outperforms existing models on multiple GUI benchmarks [28], and EASEL has been introduced as a benchmark for evaluating dexterous visual tool use in multimodal agents [23].

F03.question: Vad är det absolut  senaste inom Video genereation och är det hårdvaru- eller mjukvarurelaterat?
F03.answer:
The absolute latest development in video generation according to the provided sources is PhysStream, described in [31] with a feed date of 2026-09-16. PhysStream is an autoregressive model for physics-grounded image-to-video synthesis that incorporates structured scene memory (positional maps and object tracking maps derived online from previously generated frames) and supports fine-grained motion control via sparse velocity-increment signals [31].

PhysStream is software-based, not hardware-related. It focuses on improving video generation through advanced software architecture and algorithms rather than hardware improvements. The paper mentions it reduces motion distribution distance (FVMD) by 33% and trajectory error by 12% over baselines on synthetic benchmarks, with human evaluators preferring it in over 85% of in-the-wild comparisons [31].

The next most recent video generation development is LynnReal-Omni from [29] (2026-09-15), which is also a software-based framework for native multimodal video generation. It uses a 32B shared multimodal diffusion transformer and includes a Flash version that reduces inference cost with a lightweight VAE decoder, taking 377 ms for warm generation and decoding of a 22-frame 540p video on a single H100 [29].

Both developments are software-focused, with no mention of hardware-related innovations in the most recent video generation sources provided.

F06.question: Vad är det senaste inom benchmarking av coding agents?
F06.answer:
The latest development in benchmarking coding agents is ModularRSI, a framework introduced in [32] with a feed date of 2026-09-16. ModularRSI proposes a benchmark-disjoint, contrastive, and modular framework for generalizable harness evolution that contrasts successful and failed trajectories for the same task, aggregating evidence across tasks to identify recurring behavioral deficiencies [32]. It decomposes the evolvable harness into five functional modules: Agent Loop, Tool Use, Observation Management, Context Management, and Task Completion Detection, with each module evolving independently within a restricted modification scope [32]. The framework uses 2,000 executable evolution tasks from external sources that are disjoint from downstream evaluation benchmarks, showing consistent improvements on unseen in-domain and cross-domain tasks, with the evolved harness also transferring across different foundation models [32].

Other recent benchmarking developments include SWE-Bench Pro Verified [15] (2026-09-10), which addresses reliability issues in existing software engineering agent benchmarks by eliminating reward hacking and correcting task quality issues, and Real Suite [20] (2026-09-13), which tests AI's ability to handle actual software engineering work by giving agents access to private company code and asking them to make business-impacting changes like fixing invoice taxes or migrating customer accounts [20].

F07.question: Vad säger forskningen om text-to-video den senaste månaden?
F07.answer:
Based on the provided sources, research on text-to-video in the last month includes several key studies:

Temporal Context Routing (TCR) improves script-driven audio-video generation by mapping script timing onto the shared temporal axis of video and audio generation, routing prompt guidance to corresponding positions in both modalities. TCR reduces Shot Boundary MAE by 96% (from 1.11s to 0.042s) and raises Dialogue Acc@0.5s from 28.3% to 84.1% compared to baseline [22].

FIRM-Video introduces a unified checklist-driven framework for text-to-video reward modeling based on a "check-before-score" principle. It constructs dimension-specific checklists, verifies criteria against visual evidence, and aggregates verified decisions. The framework includes FIRM-Video-90K with 88,044 dimension-specific instances from 29,348 videos and FIRM-Video-Bench with 750 human annotations across 250 videos [29].

DF26 establishes a benchmark for detecting AI-generated videos containing fully synthetic clips produced by recent text-to-video models. It contains 271 real and 2,420 synthetic videos from seven modern video models, revealing that human performance in detection, as well as state-of-the-art deepfake detectors, is close to random chance [31].

LEGO-RL is a framework that bridges native coding-agent harnesses with scalable policy-gradient optimization without modifying the harness's internal control flow. F11.question: Vad hände i forskningen förra veckan?
F11.answer:
Based on the provided sources covering the period from 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-17, several key research developments emerged:

Multiple new benchmarks were introduced for specialized AI evaluation, including MetroLLM-Bench for testing language models as transit kiosk policy layers [4], which showed Qwen 3.5 student models exceeding GPT-5.6 tiers on Tier 1 evaluation (91.3 against 90.6 and 90.0) [4]. ReactHuman was introduced as the first physics-grounded benchmark for human-like reactive decision-making, revealing that models mishandle roughly one hazard in three when facing sudden physical hazards [5].

The paper ModularRSI proposed a modular framework for generalizable harness evolution, decomposing the evolvable harness into five functional modules (Agent Loop, Tool Use, Observation Management, Context Management, and Task Completion Detection) [1]. Lightning Weave was introduced as a post-training framework that improves the accuracy-efficiency frontier of reasoning models, raising HMMT 2025 accuracy from 59.2% to 64.0% with 10.7% fewer response tokens [13].

E2A-Bench revealed three hidden failures in financial chart reasoning: the lowest-UCR model ranked near the bottom by NDR due to only 6.4% directional coverage, oracle-aided verification could collapse coverage, and financial fine-tuning amplified the BUY:SELL ratio by factors of 4.21 to 4.68 [7]. ScienceBuddy was released as an interactive scientific research workspace implementing recursive-in-recursive self-improvement, coupling harness evolution with model reinforcement learning [26].

Convergent Emergence of In-Context Learning Across Modalities demonstrated that few-shot ICL emerges across six modalities (language, genome, integer sequences, time series, images, and proteins), supporting the Convergent Emergence Hypothesis in some modalities [18]. Drift-Constrained Optimization showed that fine-tuning is not just about how much a model changes, but how that change is spent, substantially improving scientific reasoning and multilingual translation [19].

F15.question: Vad har hänt med AI-agenter den senaste veckan, i både papers och videor?
F15.answer:
This week has seen significant developments in AI agents across both research papers and videos:

Several new agent frameworks were introduced, including "HazardAuditor" [7], which creates safer computer-use agents by normalizing interactions into a canonical event representation for cross-framework supervision. "RSIAgent" [18] enables autonomous exploration and recursive self-improvement in new environments through a multi-agent framework that constructs memory without updating model parameters.

In research, "Agent as Policy" [11] demonstrated that general-purpose agents can directly drive physical robots without task-specific training, achieving success rates up to 100% on manipulation tasks. "Atria Dawn Preview" [22] is a foundation agentic model designed for scientific research and engineering workflows, achieving top scores on five benchmarks.

The videos highlighted practical agent applications, such as "Claude Code" [9] as a skill that drives computer use through screen control and PowerShell, and "AI software factories" [4] using GPT-6 Astra that can build applications autonomously. Stripe [28] is building infrastructure for agents to make purchases (like buying coffee), though trust levels are still developing.

Multiple sources [15, 20] discussed how agents could become the primary interface for users, potentially shifting user loyalty from device manufacturers to AI companies. "Omarchy" [6] was presented as a desktop environment that makes desktop behavior accessible to agents through configuration and tooling.

Safety concerns were addressed with "Emergence World" [25], a multi-agent environment for adversarial stress testing of long-horizon autonomous systems that revealed how individually safe agents can form systems with new failure modes.
